content: A chalazion is a small lump that forms on the eyelid due to a blockage in one of the tiny oil glands. These glands, known as Meibomian glands, are responsible for producing the fluid that lubricates the eye. There are approximately 100 of these glands located near the eyelashes, and a chalazion occurs when the duct that drains one of these glands becomes obstructed. The symptoms of a chalazion include tenderness of the eyelid, increased tearing, painful swelling on the eyelid, and sensitivity to light. The diagnosis of a chalazion is confirmed through an examination of the eyelid. In rare cases, the blockage of the Meibomian gland duct may be caused by a skin cancer. If this is suspected, a biopsy may be necessary. You should seek urgent medical care if the swelling worsens or persists for more than one month despite treatment with warm compresses. Additionally, you should contact your healthcare provider if the lump on the eyelid continues to grow or if you notice an area of eyelash loss. In most cases, a chalazion resolves on its own within about a month. The primary treatment involves applying warm compresses to the affected area for 10–15 minutes at least four times a day. This helps to soften the hardened oils that are blocking the duct, promoting drainage and healing. If the chalazion continues to enlarge, surgical removal may be necessary. This procedure is typically performed from underneath the eyelid to avoid leaving a scar on the skin. Antibiotic eye drops are often prescribed for use before and after the surgical removal of the cyst, but they are not particularly effective in treating a chalazion on their own. Steroid injections are another treatment option. Large chalazia can sometimes cause astigmatism due to pressure on the cornea, but this resolves once the chalazion is treated. To prevent chalazia, proper eyelid hygiene is essential, especially for individuals prone to this condition. Cleaning the eyelash area with baby shampoo can help reduce the risk of duct blockages. The prognosis for chalazia is excellent, as they typically heal on their own or respond well to treatment.
